+New RPCs
+--------
+
+A new `exportwatchonlywallet` RPC creates a watchonly wallet file from an
+existing descriptor wallet. The exported file contains the wallet's public
+descriptors (with derived key caches where needed), transactions, and address
+book data, but no private keys. It can be imported on another node using the
+existing `restorewallet` RPC.

comments.body:
You made me think about it but I believe a backup would imply a full copy you can restore from — private keys and all. `exportwatchonlywallet` deliberately omits private keys. Calling it a "backup file" would suggest to users that their private keys are safe inside it, which they're not.

The fact that `restorewallet` happens to work as the import mechanism is an implementation detail (compatible file format), not a semantic equivalence.

Also, if anything, the language to keep consistent with is the `exportwatchonlywallet` RPC help text itself, which says "Creates a wallet file at the specified destination containing a watchonly version of the current wallet." The release notes echo that correctly I think. Thank you!
